doc: TIFF array I/O, and the suite's IN_ARRAY3 case paired with a 3-D output view on the way back. The values arrive flat with the dimensions as separate arguments and each runner shapes them -- Python reshapes a NumPy array, R builds an array and aperm()s it into the column-major layout rarrays.i reads, JavaScript passes {data, shape}, and Java fills a double[][][] for the typemap added for exactly this. A round trip that came back transposed would look identical in total and different element by element, which is why the values are all distinct.

cases.doc: Twenty-four distinct values as two 3x4 frames. Reading them back in the same flat order is the claim; the first and last elements and a middle slice are what a transpose would move.
One frame, so the leading dimension is 1 -- the shape a binding is most likely to drop or squeeze on the way through.
